shell.status_header: Every role sees the same stage, in the same words (owner decision 2026-10-31): a .pill.stage with the event's stage -- Not open yet, Sign-up open, Building, Entries closed, Judging, Results, Ended -- plus the next deadline as muted text. On each role's home screen (organiser Overview, participant Overview, judge Home) the full .stages track sits on the right of the bar, done/now/upcoming, read-only for participants and judges (plain spans, nothing to click). Judges also get a second pill for scoring right after the stage pill: 'Scoring open' (.pill.ok), 'Scoring locked' (.pill.warn) or 'Scoring not open' (.pill), none once the event has ended. Organisers keep the join/judge Copy buttons on screens other than Overview. Phone: the track is hidden (as today), the pill or pills and the deadline stay on one line.
fixes: Retest (Grok SIM-346, round 3): a judge on an event that ended without ever being locked (archived, judging_locked_at never set) saw the status pill read 'Scoring not open', as if scoring had simply never started -- it now reads 'Event ended' first, checked before the locked/open/not-open wording.

Retest (Grok SIM-346, round 1 S15): a signed-in person opening an event they're not part of (or that was deleted) gets an in-app 'Event not found' card instead of the generic error catch -- only for 404 event_not_found, guarded against a superseded navigation.

Retest (round 6, Confusing #1): resolveRoute's role (nav.js), derived only from the URL's own /manage|/team|/judge segment, was never checked against the signed-in person's real event.role -- an organiser opening a participant's /team link (a shared link, a stale bookmark, Back) rendered that participant's screen instead of bouncing to their own area. app.js's route() now compares the two and redirects (go(href(real_role, slug))) on a mismatch.

Retest (round 5, Cosmetic 2): the 404 above looks identical whether the event is truly gone or this signed-in person simply isn't (or isn't any more) a member of it -- a participant who left and later opened an old /e/<slug>/team link saw 'Event not found' about an event that still exists. route() now falls back to the credential-less public feed (GET .../public, no membership needed) on that 404: found there, it shows "You're not in <event>" with Home and Find a hackathon instead of the generic not-found card.
shell.collapsible_sidebar: 56px rail: event marks retain full title and membership-role accessible names/tooltips; expanding restores names and group labels.

layout_rules.rhythm: One 4px scale. Page header to first block 20px. Block to block 16px. Card padding 16px 18px. Sub-page heading to its card 16px. Field to field 16px. Label to control 6px. Control to help or error 6px. Section label 24px above, 8px below. Buttons in a group 8px apart. List rows at least 52px (56px with a thumbnail). kit.css .field now uses these values (was 14/4/4).
layout_rules.buttons: Exactly one primary (red) button per sub-page or dialog. A form's Save is bottom-right in .card-foot, Discard (quiet) to its left, status text far left; long forms make the foot sticky (pinned on a phone). A list's Add is top-right beside the heading (.sp-head), so it never moves as the list grows; an empty list shows its Add once, inside the empty state. Row actions sit at the row's right: quiet Edit, then the … menu, with any destructive item last and red, separated by a rule. Dialog actions bottom-right: Cancel (quiet) then the primary; full width on a phone. Destructive actions never sit next to a primary.
layout_rules.inputs: No bare file inputs: a kit button (label.btn) opens the picker and a preview sits beside it. Choices of a few known options are swatches, segmented controls or choice cards, not selects. Errors sit directly under their control in red, with aria-invalid and aria-describedby; the form keeps what was typed.
layout_rules.applies_to: Every screen built from now on. Existing screens adopt it when next touched.

decisions.q: Should judges and participants see the event's stage in the top bar?
decisions.decision: Yes, the same pill and words as the organiser on every screen, and the same read-only stage track on their home screen. The judge's scoring state moves to a second pill beside it instead of replacing the stage.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: 'For the organiser on the top it shows the current event status, but for the judge and the participant it doesn't. It should show the same thing.' This overrides the 2026-10-30 rule that a judge's pill reads only Open or Locked.

You can edit it first.', an editable Title input and Body textarea prefilled with a suggested message for that move (stage-announce.js's suggestedAnnouncement; e.g. open: 'Sign-up is open' / 'Sign-up is open. Join with the event link and find a team.', archived: 'The event has ended' / 'The event has ended. Thanks for taking part. The event page stays up as a record.'; a backward Change-stage move gets its own wording, e.g. closed backward: 'Entries are closed' / 'Entries are closed. Teams with extra time can still edit.', judging backward: 'Judging has reopened' / 'Judging has reopened. Entries stay as they are.' instead, never promising scoring reopens by itself), the same 'Email N participants' checkbox the Announcements screen uses (off by default, disabled with its explanation when emailable_participants is 0), and two buttons, 'Don't send' and 'Send'. For End event, the event archives after this dialog closes, and the announcement posts (when Send was chosen) before the archive call -- the server refuses an announcement on an already-ended event.

decisions.q: Keep the first-visit walkthrough dialog?
decisions.decision: Drop the blocking dialog; keep the underlying preference reachable from the sidebar's persistent Help link, which replays the same guidance as a dismissible panel, not a screen-covering modal.
decisions.why: Critique item 10: dropping the tour is fine, but organiser_walkthrough_done is a real stored, AI-app-reachable preference and needs a home, not a silent removal. Help already exists in the kit's side-foot for exactly this.

decisions.decision: A banner state on every organiser screen (declared once here, applies everywhere), not a separate screen.
decisions.why: Critique §4: it's cross-cutting, not a destination; declaring it as a universal state keeps one definition instead of repeating it eight times.

decisions.q: How does the new guided tour replace the old modal walkthrough panel?
decisions.decision: Guided walkthrough replaces the old modal tour: non-modal, points at real elements, shown once, replay from Help.
decisions.why: The old modal tour once blocked the judge's Score button and dialogs hide the page.

decisions.q: Why does the tour card dock at the bottom on phone instead of floating next to its target?
decisions.decision: On phone the card always sits as a bar along the bottom, clear of the step's target and the rest of the screen, with that space reserved (so whatever would sit underneath can always be scrolled to, never left stuck behind the card). On desktop it still sits beside or below its target, or in the content area's corner when the step has none.
decisions.why: Prod full test (2026-11-02): the old target-relative placement could land the card on top of a real button on a short screen -- Playwright's own click log showed #leave-btn (Home's Leave event) hidden behind .tour-card, and the welcome step covered the entry checklist the same way. There is still no dark overlay; the card itself just can't be the thing in the way any more.

decisions.q: What does the one next-step button do?
decisions.decision: It performs the next forward move itself, after one confirm, using the same effect sentences as the stage picker (FORWARD_EFFECT). Draft -> Open sign-up, Open -> Start building, Building -> Close entries, Entries closed -> Start judging, Judging -> Finish judging (moves to Results and locks judging), Results -> Publish results, published -> End event.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: 'One main button that moves the event forward. And let the Change stage be there on top.' The card's sentence explains the button, so it needs no other buttons.

decisions.q: SIM-382: where does "choose entry rules" fit into Draft -> Open sign-up?
decisions.decision: It's a step before that move, not part of it: a brand-new event's next step is 'Choose what teams hand in' (next_step.kind entry_rules), and its button navigates to Entries' handin card instead of calling the stage API -- no confirm, since nothing is saved by clicking it. Once the organiser saves a choice there, even the unchanged default, the next step becomes the ordinary Draft -> Open sign-up move above.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-11-05/06: every new event should ask what teams hand in before sign-up opens, but the asking itself isn't a stage move and has nothing to confirm -- only the save on Entries does.

decisions.q: How do Judging, the lock and Results fit into one button?
decisions.decision: Moving to Results now locks judging on the server, in the same transaction, when it is not locked yet. So Judging has one forward move (Finish judging), Results has Publish results, and publishing never meets an unlocked event at Results. Unlocking stays on the Judging screen. Going back from Results to Judging with Change stage leaves the lock on, and the picker says so: 'Judging stays locked. Unlock it on Judging to let judges score again.'
decisions.why: Results already stops scoring (scoringStage), so the lock only records what the stage already means. Without it the Results screen refused to publish an unlocked event, a dead end the one button would walk straight into.

decisions.q: Where does the next step come from, the screen or the server?
decisions.decision: The server: the organiser's event view gains next_step {kind: stage|publish_results|none, stage, label, blocked}. Overview renders it and AI apps read the same field through hack_get_event, so both say the same next move.
decisions.why: Parity rule (2026-10-27): every step works from an AI app too. One source keeps the website and the connector from drifting.

decisions.q: Keep the danger-zone End event?
decisions.decision: Yes, for ending early, except once the next-step button is End event itself (no duplicate) and once ended.
decisions.why: Ending an abandoned event before results is a real need, and the danger zone keeps it out of the main path.

decisions.q: What happened to the shortcuts the card used to hold (Review applications, See entries)?
decisions.decision: Gone from the card. Pending approvals already show as the People count in the sidebar and as a heads-up in the Start building confirm.
decisions.why: Owner: no checklist, one button.

decisions.q: Should Overview block moving to Judging while a team has no track in panel mode (audit item 2, 2026-11-02)?
decisions.decision: Warn, don't block. Name the affected teams on the card itself before Start judging is even clicked, repeat the count in the confirm, and link to Teams so the organiser can fix it there or move on anyway.
decisions.why: Picked over blocking: an organiser may want to start judging the tracked teams right away and assign the rest later, or simply decide not to judge an abandoned team. Silent dropping (today's behaviour) was the actual bug, not the ability to proceed.

decisions.q: Does the schedule move the stage at its time? (owner, 2026-11-02)
decisions.decision: Never. The server adds next_step.cue (the latest row lining up with the move whose time has come, with the wording) and Overview asks. AI apps read the same cue through hack_get_event. A delayed kickoff therefore never closes entries early.
decisions.why: Owner 2026-11-02: it never acts by itself, it only prompts, and the organiser presses the button.

decisions.q: Should every stage change offer to tell participants? (owner, SIM-341, 2026-11-05)
decisions.decision: Yes, after the move itself succeeds, not before: a dialog with an editable Title/Body prefilled from a per-move suggestion, the Announcements screen's own email checkbox and wording, and 'Don't send' / 'Send' (Escape and the scrim both mean Don't send). For End event specifically, the announcement (when Send is chosen) posts before the archive call, since the server refuses one on an already-ended event; every other move posts after. organiser-results's own Publish results (and Publish again, on a republish) offers the same dialog before its own refresh, through the same shared helper, not a second copy. A backward move to Judging must not promise scoring reopens when judging stays locked (moving back from Results): that suggestion reads 'Results are on hold' instead of 'Judging has reopened'.
decisions.why: Owner: 'Every stage change should offer to send an announcement, with the option not to send, or to edit what is sent.' Reusing Announcements' own endpoint, checkbox and live-region wording keeps the two screens from ever describing the same result differently, and extracting the dialog itself into _stage-announce-dialog.js keeps organiser-results's offer from drifting out of step with organiser-overview's.

decisions.q: SIM-388/SIM-393 — reviewed navigation and checklists
decisions.decision: Home with stage checklist and optional Not needed, checklist-led next action then existing forward confirmation; Rubric final / Mark as final in Settings → Judging.
decisions.why: Gated review and lead decisions; supersedes conflicting earlier decisions on these controls.

editing_rules.save: Three kinds, never mixed on one sub-page. (1) Forms (Basics, About) have ONE Save in the card foot, bottom-right, disabled until something changes, with Discard beside it and the status on the left. Leaving with unsaved changes (another tab, the sidebar, Back) asks 'Discard your changes to Basics?' [Keep editing] [Discard]; closing the browser tab uses beforeunload. (2) Lists (Schedule, Sponsors, FAQ) save per item: the Add/Edit dialog's Save writes straight away, a move writes straight away, Remove writes straight away with Undo in the toast. Nothing in a list waits for a page-level Save. (3) Single choices (icon, colour, Show entries, which website shows) save on change with a 'Saved' tick beside them.
editing_rules.content_writes: Schedule, Sponsors and FAQ share PUT /content. Each list write sends the latest server copy of all three arrays with only this one change applied, then replaces the local copy with the response -- never a copy assembled from other sub-pages' unsaved state. If the first GET /content fails, list sub-pages show a .note.bad with Reload and no Add, Edit or menu (the existing contentError guard).
editing_rules.urls: ?s=event-page&tab=<basics|about|schedule|sponsors|faq|look|website>. A tab click is history.pushState + re-render of the right column only (the sub-nav stays, scroll goes to the top of the content). A missing or unknown tab lands on Basics via replaceState, so Back never loops. Back/Forward re-render the tab in the URL. document.title is '<Sub-page> · Event page · <event>'. Old links still land: #basics, #schedule, #sponsors, #faq -> that tab; #appearance -> look; #address -> website; #announcements or tab=announcements -> ?s=announcements (replaceState).
editing_rules.focus_and_keys: After a tab change focus moves to the sub-page h2 (tabindex -1). The sub-nav is a nav of links with aria-current. Dialogs trap focus, Escape cancels, focus returns to the button that opened them. The row menu is a menu button (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded), arrow keys move inside it, Escape closes it. The grip is a button: Up/Down arrow moves the row one place and saves, and a polite live region says 'Kopi Kode moved to position 2 of 3'. After Remove, focus goes to the next row's Edit, or to Add when the list is empty.
editing_rules.data_loading: Entering Event page loads /content and /website once; switching tabs does not refetch. Every save refreshes only what it changed.
editing_rules.read_only: Admin view: everything is read-only on every sub-page. After End: Basics, About and Look's colour and ‘Show entries’ switch stay editable, with the note ‘This event has ended. You can still fix the page text and colour.’; Schedule, Sponsors, FAQ, the event icon and Website show values as text with no controls, because the server rejects those writes once the event is archived (see decisions).
editing_rules.custom_site_note: While your own website is live, Basics, About, Schedule, Sponsors and FAQ each carry one .note.info under their heading: 'Your own website is live at your address. This still saves, and shows again if you switch back to the built-in page.'

decisions.q: One long page with a jump nav, or one sub-page at a time?
decisions.decision: One sub-page at a time, each with its own URL (?s=event-page&tab=…), Back/Forward working, landing on Basics. This reverses the earlier 'one screen with an in-page jump nav' decision.
decisions.why: Owner 2026-10-30: 'Only show Basics when I click Basics, only Schedule when I click Schedule. This looks like a band-aid fix, clean it up.' Each piece is set up at a different time, so the page should open on exactly that piece.

decisions.q: Which sub-pages?
decisions.decision: Seven: Basics, About, Schedule, Sponsors, FAQ, Look, Website.
decisions.why: Grouped by what the organiser does in one sitting. Basics (name, tagline, dates, zone) is set once; About (about, prizes, rules, code of conduct) is long text rewritten over weeks, so it gets its own page and its own Save instead of making Basics a long scroll. Schedule, Sponsors and FAQ are lists. Look is cosmetic and safe. Website changes what the address serves.

decisions.q: Where do Announcements go?
decisions.decision: Their own organiser sidebar section, right under Event page (organiser-announcements). tab=announcements and #announcements redirect there.
decisions.why: Posting is the live-weekend action, often from a phone, and can email 148 people; everything else on Event page is set up weeks ahead. Participants already have Announcements as a section of their own, and a feed was the one thing on Event page that is not page content. One tap from the menu beats Menu > Event page > tab during the event.

decisions.q: Is Website part of Look?
decisions.decision: No, separate sub-pages.
decisions.why: Look only changes how the built-in page looks and saves on every click. Website changes what the address serves at all, has uploads and versions, and one switch that needs a confirm.

decisions.q: Where does 'Show entries on the event page' live?
decisions.decision: Look, as a switch.
decisions.why: It decides what the built-in page shows, and it is one switch like the colour and icon. Its help line says People's choice voting needs it, so an organiser setting up voting in Results knows where it is.

decisions.q: When does something save?
decisions.decision: Forms: one Save. Lists: per item, straight away. Single choices: on change. See editing_rules.save.
decisions.why: The old screen had a Save under each card and every list row was live inputs, so nobody could tell what was saved. Each kind now has one obvious rule, and a list never holds unsaved rows.

decisions.q: Edit list items in place or in a dialog?
decisions.decision: In a dialog (a bottom sheet on a phone). Rows stay one line of content.
decisions.why: Owner's screenshot complaint was rows of inputs and buttons under every sponsor. A dialog keeps the list readable, gives the form room (logo picker, two date-time pairs) and one Save.

decisions.q: Can the schedule be reordered?
decisions.decision: No reorder control. Rows are always in start-time order.
decisions.why: Both the public page (hackScheduleViews) and the participant Schedule sort by start time, so the old Move up/down on schedule rows changed nothing anyone saw. Remove is kept (reorder-remove-content-rows).

decisions.q: Confirm before Remove?
decisions.decision: No confirm for schedule items, sponsors and FAQ: Remove at once, with Undo in the toast for 10 seconds. Deleting an announcement keeps its confirm.
decisions.why: Those rows are cheap to restore. An announcement has already reached everyone's feed and maybe their inbox, which Undo cannot take back.

decisions.q: Reorder control?
decisions.decision: Drag by the grip on desktop (keyboard: arrow keys on the focused grip) plus Move up / Move down in the row menu everywhere.
decisions.why: Drag is fastest with a mouse; the menu works on a phone and for anyone who doesn't drag, without putting two buttons on every row.

decisions.q: Sub-page navigation on a phone: tabs or a select?
decisions.decision: Tabs that scroll sideways, the current one scrolled into view.
decisions.why: One tap to switch, the current place always visible, and the same pattern as the public page's chips. A select hides the options behind a second tap.

decisions.q: Can the Event page be edited after the event ends?
decisions.decision: Basics, About, colour and the ‘Show entries’ switch stay editable after End, with the note ‘This event has ended. You can still fix the page text and colour.’ Sponsors, FAQ, the event icon, Schedule, Website and Announcements are read-only after End.
decisions.why: The server refuses those changes after End -- PUT /content (schedule, sponsors, FAQ), PUT/DELETE /icon, PATCH/PUT /website and posting an announcement all answer 409 event_ended/event_closed once the event is archived, while PATCH on the event itself (title, tagline, about, prizes, rules, coc_text, accent_color, gallery_open, dates, time zone) keeps working. Matching the UI to that avoids promising edits that fail. Decided 2026-10-31 (coordinator, correcting the 2026-10-30 reading, which had this backwards).

decisions.q: Where do the real deadlines live in the schedule? (owner, 2026-11-02)

Each carries 'Set in Entries' (or Basics, Results) linking to where it changes.
decisions.why: Owner 2026-11-02: a row saying submissions close at 5pm could say one time while the real deadline said another. Copying the time in would drift the first time either changed.

decisions.q: Can a schedule time move the event's stage? (owner, 2026-11-02)
decisions.decision: No. A typed row can be set to ask for a forward move when it starts ('When this starts, ask to'), and Entries due always asks to close entries, but the stage only moves when the organiser presses the button on Overview.
decisions.why: Owner 2026-11-02: a delayed kickoff must not close entries early. The schedule prompts. The organiser decides.

decisions.q: Which moves can a row ask for?

decisions.q: Do the event's dates prompt anything?

decisions.q: Where does the entry-requirements checklist and deadline live -- Settings, or here?
decisions.decision: Here, in Entries, not Settings.
decisions.why: They're entirely about entries; grouping them with the list they govern removes a run-on section from Settings and puts the control next to what it controls.

decisions.q: Presets, per-line switches, or both?
decisions.decision: Both: three presets set every line, then any line can be changed. Modes: Required, Optional, Off, and One of for the show-your-work lines. Exactly one One-of group.
decisions.why: Owner: 'All of this should be configurable', with presets for no-code, coding and ideas events. One group covers every real rule we have heard ('video or working site', 'video, site or screenshot') without a rules language.

decisions.q: What do the presets set?
decisions.decision: SIM-382 (owner, 2026-11-05/06), replacing the original three: Video or website (the default): everything on the card Required, Video and Website One of, Code Off, Screenshot Optional, Video first. Video, website and code link: everything on the card Required, Video, Website and Code link all Required (not One of), Screenshot Optional, Website first. Title is always Required; Track is ignored when the event has no tracks. The three retired presets (AI build, Coding, Ideas and design) and Custom keep their old tables for an event already on one -- they're simply no longer offered to pick.
decisions.why: Owner: the real choice organisers care about is what evidence teams must show, not the three original event-kind labels; two clear options beat three overlapping ones plus an implicit fourth (Custom).

decisions.q: What happens to existing events?
decisions.decision: Kept exactly as they were (SIM-382): an event already on a retired preset keeps its rules and saved values, shown on Entries with neither current preset card selected; it switches only if the organiser picks Video or website or Video, website and code link. Historically, the migration had turned each pre-existing event's entry_required list into a Custom rule set (those lines Required, every new line Optional, no One-of), with Video first, and new events started on AI build; new events now start on Video or website instead, not yet chosen (entry_rules_chosen false) until the organiser saves on Entries.
decisions.why: Existing events keep exactly what they asked for; only the Submit step is new to them. No real events exist yet (owner, 2026-10-31), so the conservative mapping costs nothing.

decisions.q: Can rules change after teams submit?
decisions.decision: Yes until entries close; submitted entries stay submitted and their teams are told what's now asked for. The confirm names the counts. Read-only once the stage is Closed or later.
decisions.why: Un-submitting entries behind a team's back the night before the deadline would be the worst outcome; telling them keeps the organiser in charge without breaking anyone's work.

decisions.q: Where does Reminder times live? (notices contract, 2026-11-05)
decisions.decision: On Entries, right under the Deadline card, not on Settings. The note under it reads "Teams without a submitted entry are emailed this long before their deadline. Judges with teams left to score are reminded this long before judging closes." and names a link to Judging when judging_ends_at isn't set yet.
decisions.why: One offsets list drives both the entry-deadline reminder and the judging-closes reminder, but Entries is already 'where organisers set deadlines' -- the screen's own h1 subtitle. Settings holds organiser identity, applications and webhook notifications, none of it deadline-shaped; putting a deadline control there would be the odd one out, not this one.

decisions.q: Does a conflicted judge's earlier score still count toward the team's computed result?
decisions.decision: No -- answered from code, not left open. A declared conflict excludes that judge-team pair's score from both coverage and the team's computed total/rank, with no time qualifier.
decisions.why: computeResultsWithOptions (internal/handler/hack_judging_math.go:83-96) and ScoreCoverage (internal/db/hack_judging.go:282-302) both filter every raw score through the same EligibleJudgeTeams map (internal/db/hack_judging_options.go:64-82), which excludes any judge-team pair with a declared conflict. This was previously left in open_questions as unresolved; it isn't a product judgement call, it's a traceable fact, now reflected directly in this screen's mid-judging-conflict state copy.

decisions.q: Can an organiser drop a departed judge's scores?
decisions.decision: Yes: Delete scores on that judge's row, with a confirm, while judging is not locked. It deletes the score rows and the former-judge record.
decisions.why: Remove person can't reach someone who already left. Without this a judge could score unfairly, leave, and make those scores untouchable. Deleting (rather than hiding) stops the scores coming back if the judge later rejoins with the judge link.

decisions.q: Where is judging_ends_at set? (notices contract, CHANGE 2026-11-05)

It drives the judging-closes reminder (Reminder times, on Entries) and shows as a fixed, read-only 'Judging closes' row on the Event page's Schedule.
decisions.why: The CHANGE note dropped the original plan to infer it from a schedule row ('Finish judging') -- it is now a plain organiser-set field, like submission_deadline, so it needs a plain field, and this is the screen where the rest of judging gets set up before entries even close.

decisions.q: Is keeping 'Voting & directory' as one card inside Results the right final shape, given voting can run alongside judging, not just after it?

It is not evidence of how organisers actually use the voting controls in practice, since no usage analytics exist to check. Keeping voting inside Results for v0 stays a reasonable, reorganise-not-invent compromise; revisit with a dedicated nav item only if real usage shows organisers reaching for it mid-event often enough to justify an 8th-to-9th nav item.

decisions.q: Should every page on the site use the same save convention?
decisions.decision: Checkboxes and single toggles autosave, everything else gets one visible Save button per section -- with one explicit exception.
decisions.why: Atlas flagged three different save conventions on one tab; two patterns everywhere is simple to hold consistently. The exception: judge-scoring keeps per-tap autosave on every point chip, with no Save button at all, because that's a deliberate, load-bearing design already in the product (domain truth F.3) for judges scoring standing up on a phone -- this rule does not apply there. See judge-scoring's own decisions.

decisions.q: Where does the applications switch live?
decisions.decision: Settings, in its own card right under Organiser, saved instantly like every single toggle. People -> Sign-up shows its state in one line with a link here.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: the organiser can turn applications off in Settings. It is an event-wide 'who can ask to join' rule, not a per-person decision, so it sits with the event's identity rather than in the review queue.

decisions.q: Default for the switch?
decisions.decision: On, for every event including ones that already exist (the column defaults to true).
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: applications are on by default for every event. Flagged to the owner: existing open events gain an Apply button the day this ships.

decisions.q: How does the event creator leave while other organisers remain?
decisions.decision: They pick one co-organiser to take over (choice cards, pre-selected when there is only one). events.created_by moves to that person in the same transaction as the leave. Only a current organiser of this event can be picked, never a judge or participant.
decisions.why: Owner, SIM-340. The creator is the one organiser nobody can remove, so the event keeps exactly one while organisers remain.

decisions.q: What does the last organiser see?
decisions.decision: 'You're the only organiser' with End the event, Delete the event and Cancel. End is offered only when someone has joined (the existing archive_needs_participants rule), Delete asks for the address name typed, as Delete this event does. Either way they are not left as a member. The line about inviting a co-organiser first is the way out for someone who wanted a successor.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-30: 'If the organiser is exiting and there is no other organiser left, it should tell them this will close the event.' Ending without a member means nobody can change the ended event later, which the End card says.

decisions.q: What if two organisers leave at the same moment, or someone joins while the dialog is open?
decisions.decision: The server takes the event row FOR UPDATE, then works out the case and refuses a request built for another case. The dialog reloads and redraws. The second of two simultaneous leavers gets the last-organiser choice.
decisions.why: SIM-340: never leave the event orphaned. The server decides which case applies under a lock on the event row (GET .../leave previews it, POST .../leave repeats every check), so the dialog never has to trust what it showed earlier.

decisions.q: Does the successor's active-event limit apply to a handover?
decisions.decision: No. EVENT_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_ORGANISER is not checked on handover. The event counts toward the successor's limit from then on, which only affects what they can create next.
decisions.why: Handing over is not creating an event. With the limit at 2 by default a check would block ordinary handovers to a busy co-organiser, and it would add no protection because spare accounts can bypass a per-account creation limit anyway.

decisions.q: Where does Leave sit, and what about an ended event?
decisions.decision: In the Danger zone above Delete this event (the most destructive item goes last). On an ended event it stays visible, disabled, with the reason.
decisions.why: SIM-340: danger-zone section, and 'say why instead of hiding the button'. The layout rule puts the most destructive item last.

decisions.q: SIM-388/SIM-393 — reviewed navigation and checklists
decisions.decision: Use reviewed shared-map destinations and sections above; retain existing saves, stage locks, exports and operational actions. The desktop event list is the switcher, including clickable marks when collapsed; phone keeps the header switcher. Inspection shows separate read-only organiser navigation. Completed checklist rows have no optional controls, and phone row actions are compact below labels.
decisions.why: Gated review and lead decisions; supersedes conflicting earlier decisions on these controls.

decisions.q: Does Home need its own guided walkthrough?
decisions.decision: Yes, same rule as organiser/judge: welcome, the status bar, the next-step block, then every sidebar item (Schedule, Announcements, Team, Entry, Website, Results -- Results itself only appears once results are published, so its step already skips before then), then Help. Auto-starts once per approved participant; seen-state is localStorage (no server field for it).
decisions.why: Every role gets a Home walkthrough under the same owner rule (2026-10-30) that triggered the judge Home fix: explain only what is on screen, skip a step with no target.

decisions.q: Why does the tour card dock at the bottom on phone instead of floating next to its target?
decisions.decision: On phone the card always sits as a bar along the bottom, clear of the step's target and the rest of the screen, with that space reserved (so whatever would sit underneath can always be scrolled to, never left stuck behind the card). On desktop it still sits beside or below its target, or in the content area's corner when the step has none.
decisions.why: Prod full test (2026-11-02): the old target-relative placement could land the welcome step's card right over the entry checklist on a short screen. There is still no dark overlay; the card itself just can't be the thing in the way any more.

decisions.q: Can a participant leave after entries close?
decisions.decision: A participant on a team can leave until their team's own deadline passes, extensions included, and only in Draft, Open or Building. After that the button stays, disabled, with the reason and 'ask an organiser'. A participant with no team can leave at any stage until the event ends.
decisions.why: The handed-over spec (workspace-3 _hackleave.md) says blocked after the submission deadline so results can't change, and SIM-340 says the participant leaves the team 'with the same rules as Leave team', which already freezes a team at its deadline. The two agree. A teamless participant has no entry or score tied to them, so nothing in the results can move when they go. Organisers keep Remove person for anything later.

decisions.q: What happens to a lone member's team, entry and site?
decisions.decision: They are deleted with the team, exactly as Leave team does today (the site goes to Recently deleted, then the existing sweep purges it). The confirm says so and its button reads 'Delete team and leave'.
decisions.why: Before the deadline an empty team has nobody to publish, edit or answer for its entry, and keeping it would show judges an entry nobody owns. After the deadline the last member can't leave, so a submitted entry is never orphaned by this.

decisions.q: Can a pending applicant withdraw?
decisions.decision: Yes, through the same leave call, worded 'Withdraw application'. The pending row goes with its answers, city, country, age range and gender. They can apply or use the join link again while sign-up is open, under the usual caps.
decisions.why: Someone who applied by mistake should not have to wait for a decision to take it back, and deleting the row is what removes their personal answers. The re-apply caps (20 pending per person, the per-event cap, the apply rate limit) already bound any withdraw-and-apply churn.

decisions.q: Can a rejected applicant leave?
decisions.decision: Yes (owner decision 2026-10-31, superseding the earlier No): leaving deletes the row exactly like a pending applicant's withdraw.
decisions.why: The owner widened this twice on 2026-10-31: any member can leave any time before the event ends, and a rejected applicant is not an exception -- there is no extra machinery to stop a second application. POST .../apply after leaving creates a brand-new pending row, and the organiser decides it on its own merits, same as any first-time applicant.

decisions.q: Are teammates or organisers told?
decisions.decision: No new notice or email. Teammates see the roster change on Team, organisers see the person gone from People. Unsent announcement emails and entry receipts queued for the person are dropped, and their site notification subscriptions end (the existing trigger).
decisions.why: Owner rule for this ticket: no new notification unless one already exists, and none exists for Leave team. This replaces SIM-340's 'teammates are told', which has no mechanism behind it today.

decisions.q: How does someone come back?
decisions.decision: As a new member: the join link or Apply while sign-up is open, with the usual approval rules. The old team is not restored and the sign-up answers are asked again.
decisions.why: Leaving deletes the membership row, so there is nothing to restore, and a fresh row keeps every existing join rule in force.

decisions.q: How does an admin notice a join request?
decisions.decision: Home's next-step card says so when nothing more urgent applies, and the sidebar's Team item shows the pending count to admins only.
decisions.why: Only admins can now say yes, so the request has to reach them without anyone else nudging.

decisions.q: How does the schedule nudge a participant? (owner, 2026-11-02)
decisions.decision: One line on Home (and Schedule), in the app only: '<item> starts in N minutes' from 15 minutes before, '<item> is on now' during it. The schedule sends no email of its own.
decisions.why: Owner 2026-11-02: nudge people at the right time, ideally an in-app line. Deadline reminder emails are built separately, so the schedule must not send a second copy.

decisions.q: Do decision emails go out now (2026-11-02)?
decisions.decision: Yes. An application's approval or rejection, a team request or invite answered, a site taken down or restored, a deadline changed and being made admin all queue an email, on top of showing in the Needs you card.
decisions.why: Audit item 7: a missed approval costs more than one email. This supersedes 'No decision email goes out yet' from the 2026-10-31 application design.

decisions.q: Is email on by default, and can it be turned off per kind?
decisions.decision: On by default, with one account-level opt-out on the Account page (email-when-waiting), not a per-kind matrix.
decisions.why: These are transactional notices about the person's own team and application. The brief allows an opt-out, and a per-kind matrix is more UI than the problem needs.

decisions.q: How often can the same kind of email arrive?
decisions.decision: At most one email per kind every 15 minutes per person, batching everything of that kind that piled up in the window, across every event.
decisions.why: Owner's brief. It also caps a request/withdraw loop at four emails an hour.

decisions.q: Do organiser emails name the applicant?
decisions.decision: No. Organisers get a count of new applications by email, never names; team admins keep seeing requester names, since they already see them on Team.
decisions.why: Least personal data in inboxes.

decisions.q: Does locking or unlocking a team send anything?
decisions.decision: In-app only (a news row on Needs you), no email.
decisions.why: Nothing to act on.

decisions.q: Does leaving a team or event notify anyone?
decisions.decision: No. Leaving still sends nothing, to the person leaving or anyone else (2026-10-31 rule kept).
decisions.why: No new notification unless one already exists, and none exists for leaving.

decisions.q: Checklist or one card?
decisions.decision: Both: the .next card stays the single next step (the first unticked step, or a higher notice such as join requests), and the Your entry card lists all four steps below it.
decisions.why: Owner: 'like Your next step for organisers, participants should know they have to submit the entry, and how to connect so they can publish a website easily.' One card says what to do now; the list shows that submitting is a step at all, which today nobody is told.

decisions.q: Who computes the ticks?
decisions.decision: The server: GET /v1/hack/events/{slug} gains progress {steps[], deadline, deadline_is_extension, submitted_at, auto}, and hack_get_team_status returns the same. Home makes no extra call for it.
decisions.why: The website, an AI app and the reminder email must say the same thing about the same team; computing the rules in three places is how they drift.

decisions.q: How does the countdown tick?
decisions.decision: Every minute; every second in the last hour. Amber under 24 hours, red under 1 hour. It targets the team's effective deadline (GREATEST of event deadline and the team's override) and names an extension when there is one. Server time offset is taken from the response Date header so a wrong phone clock doesn't lie.
decisions.why: Audit: Home showed a fixed date with no clock, and the extension was visible only by noticing a later time.

decisions.q: Can a participant submit from Home?
decisions.decision: Yes, when the draft is complete: Submit entry on the next card, with a one-line confirm. Otherwise the step's button goes to the screen that fixes the missing part.
decisions.why: The common last-hour case is 'everything is there, nobody pressed the button'. One tap from Home closes it.

decisions.q: SIM-388/SIM-393 — reviewed navigation and checklists
decisions.decision: Keep current look, heroes, fallbacks, tours and exact showEntryCard predicate; shared renderer only. Judging/results/archived or published results hide entry card, including backwards-stage combinations; Draft follows existing predicate.
decisions.why: Gated review and lead decisions; supersedes conflicting earlier decisions on these controls.

decisions.q: Should Entry and Website stay part of Team, as today, or split out?
decisions.decision: Split into their own nav items, per the brief's draft sidebar.
decisions.why: Today's single Team page mixed team administration, idea-writing and publishing; the atlas flagged the entry form buried under team-admin. Three screens, three jobs.

decisions.q: Why a new no-team screen?
decisions.decision: The side-by-side Start a team and Join a team boxes are gone. The page asks one question, 'How do you want to team up?', with three stacked choice cards that each say what happens (Ask to join a team, Join with a link or code, Start a new team), and shows only the chosen way's panel under them.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: the two equal boxes, each with a field and a button, were confusing. A choice that states its consequence ('Its admins say yes or no', 'You join straight away', 'You'll be its admin') answers the question the boxes left open.

decisions.q: Which choice is picked when the page opens?
decisions.decision: Ask to join when team finding is on and at least one team is looking, or when the person already has a pending request. Otherwise Start a new team. Join with a link or code is never the default, because a person holding a link opens the link itself.
decisions.why: Matches what most people arriving here want, without hiding the other two.

decisions.q: How is an on-team Team area laid out?
decisions.decision: Like the Event page: a sub-page list (Members, Find people, Settings) on the left, one sub-page on the right, tabs that scroll sideways on a phone. URL ?s=team&tab=members|people|settings, Members by default. The page title is the team's own name.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: Teams gets its own full design the way the Event page did. Members (who is in and who wants in), finding people, and team settings are three different jobs.

decisions.q: Where do join requests go?
decisions.decision: At the top of Members, above the member list, exactly as today's Requests to join rows (Accept, Decline). Only admins can press them. Members see the same rows with 'Waiting for an admin'.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: request handling stays on the Team page as it is for now, and only the admin rule changes.

decisions.q: What is the team link?
decisions.decision: Each team has one link, https://simple-hack.app/team/<code>, shown on Members with Copy link as the page's one primary button and the code beside it for saying out loud. Any member can copy it. Opening it joins straight away after one confirm.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: 'The team code becomes a shareable link.' Every member could already share the code, so the link changes how it travels, not who can use it.

decisions.q: What can admins do that members can't?
decisions.decision: Admins: say yes or no to join requests, lock or unlock the team, rename it, edit its Looking for note, remove members (admins included, never themselves), make or remove admins, and make a new team link. Everyone on the team: see members and requests, copy the link, invite people who are looking, cancel the team's invites, choose the track, edit the entry and website, leave.
decisions.why: The admin list is the owner's, minus the track. The track is part of the team's work, like the entry every member edits, and gating it would stop a member fixing it while the admins are away. Invites stay open to every member because every member can already share the link, which joins instantly.

decisions.q: What happens when the last admin leaves?
decisions.decision: The member who has been on the team longest becomes admin automatically, in the same transaction, whichever way the admin went (left the team, left the event, was moved or taken off by the organiser). Leave team says who it will be: 'Dian becomes admin when you leave.' An admin can't step down while they are the only one.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: the oldest member becomes admin automatically. A team never sits without someone who can approve requests.

decisions.q: Who is admin on teams that already exist?
decisions.decision: Whoever started the team, if still on it, otherwise the member who joined it first. Teams placed by Fill teams: the first person placed.
decisions.why: No real events exist yet (owner, 2026-10-31), so existing teams move to the new rule directly instead of keeping everyone equal.

decisions.q: What does locking do?
decisions.decision: Lock team ('No more people can join') stops join requests, link and code joins, invites (sending and accepting) and Fill teams placement into this team. Pending requests and invites for the team are cleared when it locks, and unlocking restores nothing. The organiser can still place someone on a locked team by hand. A team kept after its last member left past the deadline is locked for good.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: a team can be locked and that blocks requests, code joins, invites and Fill teams. Clearing pending offers matches the existing rule that leaving restores nothing, and leaves no request that can only ever fail.

decisions.q: What replaces 'Who can join: Anyone / Only people with the code'?
decisions.decision: Nothing. Every team that isn't locked can be asked (it appears in Ask to join while team finding is on) and joined with its link or code. A team that wants no strangers declines requests or locks.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: remove the setting, two ways in. The old code-only teams join the list. No real events exist, so nobody's choice is overridden in practice.

decisions.q: Does turning team finding off stop admins managing their team?
decisions.decision: No. Off hides Ask to join, Find people and Let teams find you, and refuses requests and invites, as today. Links, codes, lock, rename, admins and removing members keep working, and Fill teams works too.
decisions.why: Team finding is about discovering strangers. Managing your own team, and the organiser placing people, are not discovery.

decisions.q: Does the Team screen keep its own walkthrough?
decisions.decision: Yes, rewritten for the new no-team page: the question and its three choices, Ask to join, Join with a link or code, Start a new team, and Let teams find you. Steps whose target is missing (team finding off) are skipped, as today.
decisions.why: Same owner rule (2026-10-30): a walkthrough explains only the screen it's shown on.

decisions.q: Where do organiser messages show on Team? (notices contract, 2026-11-05)
decisions.decision: A Messages from the organisers card on Members (the default tab), right under the sp-head and above the Team link card -- hidden entirely (no card at all) when the team has never been messaged.
decisions.why: Members is what everyone already lands on; a message from the organisers is exactly the kind of thing that should be seen without hunting through Settings. Hidden rather than an empty state because most teams will never get one and an always-there 'nothing here' card is just noise.

decisions.q: Should an organiser be able to hide the rubric from teams (audit item 1, 2026-11-02)?
decisions.decision: No setting. Every team always sees the rubric, the same read-only data judges and organisers already see -- never a score.
decisions.why: The rubric already exists and is harmless to read; the only blocker was hack_judging.go:96's loadMember(..., "organiser", "judge") role list, which now also accepts "participant". The card lives here (one fetch); Home only links down to it.

decisions.q: Is 'Solution, one line' a new field?
decisions.decision: No. It is the existing tagline column and JSON key, relabelled 'Solution, in one line' (160 characters, as today). New columns: problem, audience, tools, maturity.
decisions.why: Two one-liners that say the same thing would make teams write it twice. Gallery, voting and results already show the tagline, so they get the solution line with no change, and no data moves.

decisions.q: Where does the entry's track live?
decisions.decision: On the team (event_teams.track_id), as today. The entry form's Track select writes the team's track, under the Team screen's rule (any member, until the deadline). Hidden when the event has no tracks.
decisions.why: Judging panels key off the team's track. A second copy on the entry could disagree with the panel the team is judged by. The audit's 'panels drop untracked teams' problem shrinks once Track is Required on the card.

decisions.q: Tools and AI: free text or a list?
decisions.decision: Tags. Up to 10, 30 characters each, case-insensitive dedupe. Suggestions are a fixed list in two rows, AI apps then tools, and typing anything else is allowed.
decisions.why: Owner asked for 'tags with suggestions'. A fixed list keeps spelling consistent (Claude, not claude.ai) without hiding uncommon tools. Suggestions are not drawn from other teams' tags, so nobody sees a rival's stack before results.

decisions.q: What does 'what works today' offer?
decisions.decision: Three choice cards: Demo-ready (works end to end), Partly working (some parts are mocked), Concept (designs or a plan, nothing runs yet). Stored as working / partial / concept.
decisions.why: Judges calibrate 'does it work' scores against it, and in an ideas event Concept is an honest, normal answer, not a failure.

decisions.q: Does saving a draft check the rules?
decisions.decision: No. Save draft never refuses for a missing line (length and URL checks still apply). Only Submit checks, and a submitted entry's saves are checked so it can't become incomplete.
decisions.why: Teams fill the card over a weekend in pieces; blocking a save loses work. The owner's rule is about submission: 'Required must be ENFORCED when the entry is submitted'.

decisions.q: Can a team change a submitted entry?
decisions.decision: Yes, until the team's deadline, and it stays submitted. Move back to draft exists for a team that wants it out of the submitted count.
decisions.why: Hackathons keep building to the last minute. Forcing a re-submit after every edit would turn the deadline into a trap for teams that forget to press the button twice.

decisions.q: What happens at the deadline to a draft?
decisions.decision: A draft that meets every rule is submitted automatically (marked automatic). A draft that doesn't is still judged, carrying an Incomplete flag judges and organisers see. Organisers can exclude a flagged entry by hand on Entries, with a confirm. Coordinator decision 2026-11-02, replacing 'not judged'; the owner can overrule.
decisions.why: A complete entry should never miss judging over one button. Dropping an incomplete one would throw away a team's whole weekend over one missing line, so it is judged and flagged, and the organiser keeps the final say with Exclude.

decisions.q: Does the team agree to its card being public?
decisions.decision: The Entry screen says, under More detail: 'After results, your summary card, video and website can appear on the event's public page if the organisers show your entry.' No extra switch.
decisions.why: Entries are made for a public event whose results page already names teams and links their sites. Telling them before they submit is the honest part; a per-team opt-out would let a winner's card vanish from the results.

decisions.q: When is a judge done, and by when must she finish?

decisions.q: How does the new guided tour replace the old modal walkthrough panel?

decisions.q: Why does the tour card dock at the bottom on phone instead of floating next to its target?
decisions.decision: On phone the card always sits as a bar along the bottom, clear of the step's target and the rest of the screen, with that space reserved (so whatever would sit underneath can always be scrolled to, never left stuck behind the card). On desktop it still sits beside or below its target, or in the content area's corner when the step has none.
decisions.why: Prod full test (2026-11-02): the old target-relative placement could land the card on top of a real button on a short screen -- Playwright's own click log showed #leave-btn (Home's Leave event) hidden behind .tour-card on judge Home specifically. There is still no dark overlay; the card itself just can't be the thing in the way any more.

decisions.q: Should Home's walkthrough also explain the scoring page?
decisions.decision: No. Home's tour only covers what is on Home (welcome, status, the next-step block, progress, My teams, Rubric & brief, Help); the two steps that used to explain scoring there (no target, so they always showed) moved to a new tour on the scoring page itself (judgeScoring). The status step is stage-aware: it says the event is open while scoring is open, says when it opens while it isn't, and is left out entirely once judging is locked or results are out.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-30: on Home, steps 5-6 of 7 explained the scoring page while the judge was still on Home looking at nothing, and on an event whose results were already out they didn't apply at all -- scoring was over.

decisions.q: Are a departed judge's scores kept?
decisions.decision: Kept and still counted, frozen as they stood when the judge left. The server records them as a former judge of the event and counts their scores for the teams that were eligible for them at that moment (their conflicts still apply). That list of teams is stored with the record, so later changes to assignments or panels don't move their scores in or out. Their other score rows stay uncounted, as today. An organiser can delete a former judge's scores from Judging.
decisions.why: Results should not shift because a judge stepped away after doing the work (SIM-340's recommendation). Today eligibility requires membership, so a removed judge's scores silently stop counting. 'Kept' needs this record or the totals would change behind the organiser's back.

decisions.q: Can a judge leave after judging locks, or after results?
decisions.decision: Yes, at any stage until the event ends, with the scores kept and counted.
decisions.why: Locking freezes scores and the published results are a stored snapshot, so leaving changes nothing in either. A judge who is done should be able to clear the event from their Home.

decisions.q: How does a judge come back?
decisions.decision: With the judge link until results are published. Rejoining removes the former-judge record and their kept scores count as a member's again.
decisions.why: Same link rule as today, and the person is the same account, so their scores are theirs again.

decisions.q: What does the top bar say for a judge?
decisions.decision: The event's stage like everyone else (pill plus the track on Home), then a scoring pill: Scoring open, Scoring locked or Scoring not open. Nothing else on judge screens changes.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31, top bar for judges and participants. The judge UX is otherwise fine, so this is the only judge change.

decisions.decision: 'I know this team' opens a real confirm dialog, never a hover hint, naming the team (never the entry) throughout, matching the undo dialog in judge-queue. decisions.decision: 0–10 buttons are at least 44 px tall and wrap to two rows on a phone, and a 'Go to scoring' link under the team's name jumps past the website preview.
decisions.why: Walkthrough measured 28×37 px chips and 620 px of scrolling between the site and the scores.

decisions.q: Where does the scoring walkthrough live, and when does it start?
decisions.decision: Its own tour (judgeScoring), auto-starting the first time a judge opens scoring while it's actually open and editable (not on a locked/read-only visit). It points at the team's website link, the first criterion's score buttons, the comment box, Save & next, "I know someone on this team", and Previous. Seen-state is localStorage, not the preferences API (which only has judge_walkthrough_done).
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-30: walkthroughs explain only what is on screen, so scoring is explained on the scoring page, not from Home. Only a locked visit has none of these controls to point at, so it doesn't auto-start there.

decisions.q: In what order does a judge see an entry?
decisions.decision: Card, then the event's first medium (Video by default, Website for the Video, website and code link preset), then the other, then code and More detail. The organiser chooses Video or Website first in Entries; the card is always first.
decisions.why: Owner: 'Judges see it first, then the video if there is one, then the website. Website and video can be interchangeable. A coding hackathon can be different.'

decisions.q: Can the video play on the scoring screen?
decisions.decision: Yes for YouTube (as youtube-nocookie.com), Vimeo, Loom and Google Drive: the server parses the ID with a strict pattern and returns video.embed_url; the page loads the iframe only when the judge presses play, with no autoplay. The app CSP adds exactly those four frame hosts. Every other host is a large link naming the host.
decisions.why: A 2-minute video in another tab breaks the one-screen flow, but a raw user URL must never become an iframe source. Click-to-load keeps third parties out until the judge asks, and keeps the screen fast.

decisions.q: Can the live site be framed?
decisions.decision: Yes, from the team's own origin, as a preview: the frame always loads the server's site.preview_url, the submitted (pinned) version once the team is pinned and a preview of the live version before, never the bare live address. Only the judge route (/e/{slug}/judge) is served with the wider CSP (hackAppCSP): its frame-src adds https://*.<team-sites domain> (one wildcard, not per event) and the four video players; every other app route keeps frame-src 'self' blob:, and the app reloads the page when it navigates to the judge route from one of them. Previews on the Simple Hack platform answer frame-ancestors 'self' https://<app origin>, which also overrides the proxy's X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN; a signed-in member's own pages keep frame-ancestors 'self'. sandbox allows scripts, forms, same-origin and popups (to escape the sandbox for links), never top navigation. Sites with a passcode or named viewers, offline, taken down or not ready are frameable:false with not_frameable_why, and show the screenshot, the reason in one line and Open website.
decisions.why: Team sites send no frame-ancestors, so the only blocker was the app's frame-src 'self'. Previews never get owner rights (INTENT 2026-10-10), and signed-in member pages already refuse framing by another origin. Built 2026-11-02 (slice 2): the live proxy adds X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN to every response, so previews carry their own frame-ancestors for the app origin; and the wider frame-src is limited to the judge route because only it frames anything.

decisions.q: Keyboard on desktop?
decisions.decision: N = Save and next, P = Previous, outside text fields. Shown as a small hint under the buttons. Digits are not bound.
decisions.why: A remote judge scoring 30 teams uses a laptop. Binding digits would collide with three criteria on one screen.

decisions.q: What stops a skipped criterion?
decisions.decision: The one-line guard on Save and next, not a dialog.
decisions.why: Fast flow first; a dialog on every partial score would be the very friction the owner wants gone.

decisions.q: What does the MCP App judge view show?
decisions.decision: The same screen with the card first, and the video and website as links (Watch the demo video, Open website) with the screenshot. No embeds: the App frame's own CSP is frame-src 'none'.
decisions.why: Build plan section 5: MCP App frames have their own CSP, so no embeds there in v1.

decisions.q: Are team members' names on the judge's card?
decisions.decision: No. The card names the team only, as slice 1 shipped it; the prototype's member names are not sent to judges.
decisions.why: Judges have never been sent member names (queue and MCP alike); adding them is a privacy change, left for the owner to decide.

Uses the app kit (AppURL/hack/kit.css, CSP already allows style-src from AppURL) plus a few page rules inline. Drops the site header, hack-ink.css and the theme switch (light only). Keeps the shared footer links.

Event colour: --ev is the organiser's colour for the header rule, stage card border, icon fallback and letter marks. --accent for buttons and links is color-mix(in srgb, --ev 50%, #000), the same AA rule hack-ink.css uses today, declared after a plain brand-red fallback so old Android browsers without color-mix still get a readable accent.

Head: title '<Title> · Simple Hack', meta description and og:description = tagline (fallback: stage words), og:title, og:type website, og:image = IconURL (not when taken down), twitter:card summary. noindex for draft and taken down as today.

fixes: Hand-drawn ink look, tilted cards and a dark-mode switch replaced by the app kit's calm straight style, light only, still themed by the event colour and icon.

'Anyone can join. No coding needed.' was shown on every open or building event, also on approval-only ones. Removed, the organiser's own About and FAQ say who can join.
Results sat at the very bottom after eight sections. They now come first in Results and Ended.
The team gallery sat last. It now follows the stage card from Closed on, and has a count and one link per card.
The deadline countdown kept running in Results ('Entries are closed.'). Time left now shows only in Open and Building, a static closing time in Closed, nothing after.
Announcement dates were UTC days. They now use the event's time zone, like every other time on the page.
Multi-day schedule items showed only the end time ('Wed 28 Oct, 10:00–18:00'). The end date is shown when it is a different day.
The date line showed the zone as 'Asia/Jakarta'. It now says 'times in WIB'.
Scores read '80.00 (raw)' on every row. The method is said once above the list in plain words.
Link previews: today only og:image is set. Adds title, description and card tags so a WhatsApp or Instagram share shows the event name and tagline.
The phone page was over 3,300px with no way to jump. Adds 'On this page' chips, collapses Rules and Schedule after the event and folds older announcements.
Tracks were near the bottom. Prospects see them right after About.
'Visit sponsor' links all had the same name. Each now says 'Visit <sponsor>'.

Corrects the previous atlas entry, which promised status tags on gallery cards and a 'results expected' date. Neither exists in the data, both moved to feature ideas.

Retest (Grok SIM-346, round 2): the header's Sign in/Home swap only ever worked on the app's own origin -- localStorage.apiKey can never be read at the event's own canonical URL (the slug subdomain), so a signed-in visitor there still saw 'Sign in'. It now checks location.host against the AppURL host first: same origin keeps the old localStorage check, any other host always shows 'Sign in', linking straight at the app's sign-in page instead of the neutral Home. The schedule's own ordering is a stable sort, so same-time items keep a fixed order across loads instead of reshuffling.

Retest (Grok SIM-346, round 4): a pending or rejected applicant saw the same 'You've already joined / Continue to your event' as a full member, with Continue only leading to a second screen saying the application was still waiting (or wasn't accepted) -- the membership check now reads role and approval_status and shows 'Your application is waiting for the organisers.' with 'See your application' (pending), or 'Your application wasn't accepted this time.' with no Continue (rejected). A signed-in visitor who isn't a member of this event no longer sees 'Already joined? Sign in' -- that signal is hidden the moment we know they're signed in, independent of whether the membership check that follows finds a role.

Retest (round 5, Cosmetic 3): hiding 'Already joined? Sign in' wasn't enough -- a signed-in visitor confirmed NOT a member (the membership check 404s) still read the card's default body, 'Sign in with your email...', which makes no sense once they're already signed in. On that 404 the card now reads 'Apply' (reusing whatever Apply link the page already rendered, so it still respects applications_open) or, with no Apply on the page, 'Ask the organisers for the join link' -- no sign-in wording either way.

decisions.q: What is the main action in Open when the page cannot show the join link?
decisions.decision: A stage card titled 'Join with the link from the organisers' that says where the link usually comes from, plus a quiet 'Already joined? Sign in'. No fake Join button.
decisions.why: The view has no join URL and the app has no way to type a join code, so a button would lead nowhere. Telling a first-timer exactly what to look for is the honest next step. Showing the link is feature idea 1 for the owner.

decisions.q: One page order for all stages, or reorder by stage?
decisions.decision: Reorder by stage. The header and footer never move, the block under the header is the stage's job, and sections follow who reads the page at that stage.
decisions.why: The readers change completely: prospects and parents before, participants during, everyone looking for winners after. One fixed order buries results under eight sections, which is today's main complaint.

decisions.q: Where does 'Sign in' / 'Already joined' go?
decisions.decision: AppURL/events (Your events), not /e/<slug>/team.
decisions.why: The page cannot know the reader's role. /e/<slug>/team renders participant screens even for a judge or organiser, while Your events works for every role and returns there after sign-in.

decisions.q: Who sees the organiser identity?
decisions.decision: 'Organised by Amara Putri (Generation Girl)' sits in the header facts line on every stage, and the footer keeps Report a page.
decisions.why: A parent or teacher decides legitimacy from who runs it. Today the line is small and grey under the title.

decisions.q: What happens to sections that matter less after the event?
decisions.decision: Schedule and Rules collapse into details in Results and Ended. Nothing is removed.
decisions.why: Reorganise, do not remove. Collapsing keeps the content reachable without making the results page long on a phone.

decisions.q: Status tags on gallery cards?
decisions.decision: No tags. Cards show screenshot or letter, title, tagline, team name and one link.
decisions.why: The card data has no per-team status. The stage card and stage pill already say what is happening to every team.

decisions.q: How does the event colour theme the page without breaking contrast?
decisions.decision: Raw colour for rules, borders, letter marks and the icon fallback. A 50%-darkened mix for buttons and links, with brand red as fallback.
decisions.why: Some crayons (yellow, orange) fail as text or button colour on paper. This is the same rule the ink page uses today, so organisers see the same identity.

decisions.q: Keep the countdown?
decisions.decision: Yes, only in Open and Building, as the one nonce script. Without JavaScript the closing date and time is shown.
decisions.why: Participants mid-event want time left at a glance. The date alone is complete without the script.

decisions.q: Header nav like the app shell?
decisions.decision: No shell. A plain top bar with the wordmark, Find a hackathon and Sign in.
decisions.why: Owner direction 7: public pages stay pages. Visitors have no role and no event switcher.

decisions.q: Should Team sites show in the open stage too?
decisions.decision: Team sites show from sign-up when the gallery is on, as before (review 2026-10-30)
decisions.why: The old page showed the gallery in every stage after draft whenever the gallery switch was on, and voting can open before entries close too. layout_by_stage.open had dropped it; restored right after Tracks, the same adjacency every later stage keeps between the two.

decisions.q: What is the main action in Open now that people can apply?
decisions.decision: Apply, when the event takes applications (on by default). The card says the organisers decide and where the answer appears, and points people who have a join link to it. With applications off, the old 'Join with the link from the organisers' card returns unchanged. The join link itself is never shown.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: people without a join link apply from the event's page; join links stay private. This answers open question 1 and replaces feature idea 1 (expose the join link).

decisions.q: Does the page say whether approval is needed?
decisions.decision: Only through the Apply card's 'The organisers decide who joins'. The public data gains one boolean, applications_open, and nothing about the join-link approval setting.
decisions.why: Every application is reviewed whatever that setting is, so the sentence is always true. Keeping the public data to one fact keeps the organiser's sign-up rules private (feature idea 2 is no longer needed).

decisions.q: An organiser's own uploaded site at the event address: where is Apply?
decisions.decision: On the built-in page at simple-hack.app/e/<slug> as always. The organiser can link their own site to simple-hack.app/e/<slug>/apply; organiser-api.md says so.
decisions.why: The redesign touches only the built-in page; the apply address is stable and works from anywhere.

decisions.q: Does the public schedule show the real deadlines? (owner, 2026-11-02)
decisions.decision: Yes. The event's start and end, the entry deadline, the voting window (while voting is on) and results published are merged into the Schedule as rows, computed from the settings, so the page never shows a stale time. No prompts and no team extensions on the public page.
decisions.why: Prospects and participants check the Schedule for when things happen. The deadline is the time that matters most and must match the countdown.

decisions.q: Whose summary shows after results?
decisions.decision: Exactly the teams the results already show: winners only (overall and track winners) or every ranked team, following the existing visibility setting. Taken from the results snapshot, so moving the event back a stage never changes a published card.
decisions.why: Owner: 'When the results are out, if all entries are enabled or even only winners, you should see the summary along with the website.' Reusing the setting means no new switch and no team appears that the organiser chose not to show.

decisions.q: Is the video embedded on the public page?
decisions.decision: No. A button 'Watch video · <host>' opens it in a new tab. The public page keeps frame-src none.

decisions.q: Its own page, or a step inside the join page?
decisions.decision: Its own address, /e/{slug}/apply, and its own screen module, reusing public-join's markup for the questions and code of conduct.
decisions.why: The join page is keyed by a secret code and must keep working exactly as now (owner, 2026-10-31). An application is keyed by the public event name, has different rules (always reviewed, extra optional fields, organiser switch) and a different audience. One screen per atlas id keeps both simple.

decisions.q: Show the organiser's questions before sign-in, like public-join does?
decisions.decision: No. Before sign-in the page says what kinds of things are asked; the questions and the organiser's code of conduct appear after sign-in.
decisions.why: Organisers wrote those questions for people they invited with a link. The public surface of this feature is one fact: whether applications are open. Signing in is one emailed code, and the form is one screen after it.

decisions.q: How are optional fields marked?
decisions.decision: '(optional)' after the label, required fields unmarked, the same convention as the join form and the organiser screens. The three new fields carry it in their labels; a group label says 'Where you're based (optional)'.
decisions.why: Most fields on this form are optional; marking the few required ones would invert the app's convention and confuse anyone who has used the join form.

decisions.q: What does an Under 18 applicant see?
decisions.decision: Exactly the same form, plus one plain sentence when Under 18 is picked: a parent or guardian needs to agree to the Terms for them. No birth date, no guardian email, no extra step.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: no extra data from minors. The Terms already say 13+ and guardian agreement under 18; the sentence only makes that visible at the moment it applies. The organiser sees Under 18 highlighted so they can follow their own safeguarding rules.

decisions.q: Which gender options?
decisions.decision: Woman or girl, Man or boy, Non-binary, Another gender, Prefer not to say -- one select, optional. No free-text self-description.
decisions.why: Applicants range from 13-year-olds to adults, so 'Woman or girl' reads right for both. A free-text box would collect more than the owner asked for and would need moderation in the organiser's list.

decisions.q: Country: free text or a list?
decisions.decision: A list of countries (ISO 3166 codes stored, names shown in the browser's own language); city is free text.
decisions.why: Organisers filter and report by country (CSR programmes count reach per country); free text gives 'Indonesia', 'indonesia', 'ID', 'RI'. No reliable city list exists, and city is only read by people.

decisions.q: Prefill these fields from a person's earlier application to another event?
decisions.decision: No. The form starts empty each time; only the name is prefilled from the account.
decisions.why: The answers belong to one event's application and are deleted with it. Carrying them across events would quietly reuse data a person gave a different organiser.

decisions.q: Should unlisted events take applications?
decisions.decision: No. Apply shows, and applications are accepted, only for events listed in Find a hackathon. An unlisted event's apply page shows the applications-off state (closed_reason not_listed).
decisions.why: An organiser who keeps an event out of the directory chose a private, join-link-only event. Owner, 2026-10-31, after the security review raised it.

decisions.q: Does a team link let someone into the event?
decisions.decision: No. It joins a team only. A person who isn't an approved participant is told why and pointed at Apply or the organiser.
decisions.why: The organiser controls who is in the event (join link, approval, applications). A team's link must not be a way around that.

decisions.q: What does a signed-out visitor see?
decisions.decision: The team's name and the event's title only, never members, so the page can say what they're about to join before sign-in. The preview is rate-limited like the event join preview.
decisions.why: Someone holding the link can join anyway, so the name tells them nothing new, while member names would.

decisions.q: One confirm, or join on open?
decisions.decision: One confirm, Join Kopi Kode. Opening a link never changes anything by itself.
decisions.why: Owner, 2026-10-31: joins automatically after one confirm. Link previews in chat apps and prefetching must not join anyone.

planned.name: Leave this event
planned.what: Designed in the atlas 2026-10-31, not built yet. Any participant, judge or organiser can leave from their Overview or Settings danger zone, or from a Home row's … menu. A participant leaves their team first (a lone member's team, entry and site are deleted) and can't leave once their team's deadline passes. A pending applicant withdraws. A judge's scores stay and still count. The creator hands the event to another organiser first. The last organiser ends or deletes the event. Nothing on an ended event.

planned.name: Entries and participant journey
planned.what: Designed in the atlas 2026-11-02, not built yet. Entry summary card (problem, solution, who it's for, track, tools and AI tags, what works today) with presets and per-line Required / One of / Optional / Off rules enforced on an explicit Submit; complete drafts submit themselves at the deadline. Judges get the card, video and live site on one screen beside the rubric. Participant Home is a four-step checklist with a live countdown to the team's own deadline. Website guides each AI app and shows Connected and Published from real data. Results and the public page show each shown team's card, site and video. Build plan: scratchpad entries-design/build-plan.md (three slices).
